title: Primary and secondary data
log: 2026-11-04T09:36:50Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: The bank has two separate Year 11 NSW cards, one on primary data and one on secondary data, written at a much greater depth (fieldwork planning, survey and interview design, source reliability checks) than the simple Year 7 definitions this point needs, so neither fits as it is and a new point is the safer match.

draft.title: Primary and secondary data
card: Data you collect yourself, first-hand. Surveys, interviews, measurements and field sketches taken during fieldwork are examples.
Data that someone else collected before you. Census figures, maps, satellite images and published reports are examples.
The same fact can be either kind. It depends on who collected it. If you count the cars yourself, it is primary. If you read a council's count, it is secondary.
Primary data answers your own question and is up to date, but it takes time to collect. Secondary data is quick to find, but it was gathered for another purpose and may be out of date.
draft.remember: Primary: you collected it. Secondary: someone else did.

a.q: Which of these is primary data?
opts: Rainfall measured with a gauge at your school
Rainfall totals from a Bureau of Meteorology table
Rainfall figures in a textbook chapter
Rainfall data in a news report about a flood
a.why: You collected the gauge readings yourself, so they are first-hand. The other three were collected by someone else and only read by you, so they are secondary data.

b.q: Amira studies how students travel to her school in Darwin. She reads last year's travel figures in a council report, then surveys her own class. Which describes her data?
opts: The report is secondary and the survey is primary
The report is primary and the survey is secondary
Both are primary because both are about her school
Both are secondary because the survey is a small sample
b.why: The council collected the report figures, so for Amira they are secondary. She collected the survey answers herself, so they are primary. Being about her own school does not make data primary, because it depends on who collected it.
b.clue: Ask who collected each set of figures, not what it is about.

a.best: Rainfall measured with a gauge at your school

b.best: The report is secondary and the survey is primary
